title: Exemplar Entropy Dossier
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for a small, messy experiment: how to intentionally inject controlled "entropy" into exemplar sets to (a) surface brittle failure modes and (b) create a small calibration bank for fallback/template selection. Not a final plan — more like a lab bench.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Slightly heterogeneous few-shot exemplars (mixing register, detail level, and minor contradictions) increase robustness to domain-shift prompts but expose new hallucination vectors. We want to characterize the trade-off and produce simple heuristics for exemplar selection that balance fidelity vs. generalization.

Design (mini-experiments):
1) Baseline (mono-register): 5 exemplars, same formal register, same length approx 80–120 tokens, consistent label format.
2) Controlled-entropy sets: 5 exemplars but vary one axis at a time: tone (formal/casual), sparsity (long/short), correctness (minor deliberate errors), and viewpoint (first/third). Create four variants where each set has a single axis varied across exemplars.
3) High-entropy scramble: 5 exemplars sampled across axes (wild mix).
4) Shot-synthesis: 3 exemplars + 2 retrieval-augmented (LLM-provided paraphrases).

Metrics to track (quick list):
- Exact-match/label accuracy (where applicable).
- Precision of factual fields (dates, names) measured by regex-driven extractors.
- Token hallucination count (heuristic: presence of confident but unsupported facts).
- Output variance (entropy) across 10 seeds per prompt.
- Latency/length and token cost (practical).

Prompt templates (working variants):
A) Instruction-first canonical: "You are an assistant that converts user notes into structured bullet summaries. Follow examples precisely." + exemplars.
B) Role-anchored: "As an editorial assistant, rewrite the input into a 3-bullet TL;DR with a one-sentence rationale." + exemplars.
C) Constraint-primed (sanity checks): "Do not add new facts. If uncertain, write \"[UNSURE]\" for that field." + exemplars.

Representative few-shot exemplars (condensed):
- E1 (formal, long): Input: "Meeting notes — product licensing model discussion..." -> Output: Bulleted summary + action items labeled with owners and dates.
- E2 (casual, short): Input: "chat w/ PM: pricing idea, try alt plan B" -> Output: 3 bullets, no owners, fuzzy date.
- E3 (formal, subtle error): Input: "client X has quota 10k" -> Output: includes quota but tags as verified: false in bracket.
- E4 (first-person vignette): Input: "I noticed the API is slower when..." -> Output: diagnostic steps + confidence score.
- E5 (third-person case): Input: "Support ticket: user cannot save settings" -> Output: root-cause hypothesis + repro steps.

Failure modes observed (expected / to monitor):
- Overfitting to exemplar length: baseline often mirrors punctuation and verbosity; scramble reduces that but increases spurious concretions.
- Cross-shot contaminations: Model invents an owner from a different example when exemplars contain owners with overlapping names.
- Confirmation hallucination: When an exemplar contains a deliberate minor error (E3), model sometimes amplifies it rather than hedge.
- Directive erosion: Constraint-primed prompts (C) work when constraints are explicit, but get ignored if exemplars use contradictory implicit patterns.

Small diagnostics to add (practical):
- Insert guard tokens: prepend "<CHECK>" to factual fields in exemplars and see whether model learns a tokenized 'do not invent' behavior. Quick A/B.
- Ownership disambiguation: canonicalize owner formats (email vs. name) in some sets to see if format consistency reduces cross-shot contamination.
- Shot provenance tag: append "[EXEMPLAR-ID: e3-corrected]" and log which exemplar the model copies from (simple string match).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be useful to pair this with a tiny reranker that penalizes outputs that add new named entities. Could be a heuristic classifier (spaCy NER differences between input+context vs. output).
- Add cheap eval harness: 50 synthetic prompts, run each exemplar set x 3 temperatures (0.0, 0.3, 0.7) -> gather per-prompt delta in factual precision.
- Consider runtime heuristics for 'entropy-aware' exemplar selection: pick the top-3 most consistent exemplars by Jaccard overlap with the input, then intentionally inject 1 higher-entropy exemplar to test resilience.

Open questions / blockers:
- Does the labeled 'uncertain' token approach actually reduce confident hallucinations or merely move them? Need to quantify.
- Are there licensing/PII risks in storing exemplars with real names (we should use synthetic or redacted tokens).
- How to represent exemplar provenance in telemetry (per-request exemplar id metadata)? Followup with backend infra team (SRE/Tracing) — ping @sre on slack.

Quick next steps (two-week sprint):
- Week 1: build the 4 exemplar-variant sets (+ baseline), implement harness and regex-based extractors. Run 500 queries across temps. Owner: Marco.
- Week 2: analyze failure clusters, run guard-token ablations, produce a short internal note w/ recommendations (3 heuristics). Owner: Aisha.

References / links to track:
- GH PR with initial harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rnd/pull/482
- Linear ticket for telemetry: LINEAR-1234
- Slack thread: #prompt-research (search: "entropy exemplars")

Scratch lines / TODOs:
- [ ] generate synthetic exemplar bank (100 variants) using templates + small randomization script (python).
- [ ] schedule 30-min sync with Marco + Yvonne to align metrics definitions.
- [ ] draft short README for the harness so infra/ops can run locally.

Small personal log: tried a 3-exemplar high-entropy set yesterday evening; model returned a confident-but-wrong customer quota in 2/5 seeds. That's a red flag — run the uncertainty-token ablation first.

End of file (for now).
